narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, your credit history, and the status of your checking account. The requested duration of 48 months was the single biggest reason for the denial. At more than twice the average length of approved loans (19 months), this long repayment period strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Your credit history of having critical or other existing credits was the second most important factor; while this actually nudged the model slightly toward approving you, its helpful effect was not large enough to overcome the other concerns. Finally, the status of your checking account (currently between 0 and 200 DM) was the third strongest driver and worked against you. Only 18% of approved applicants have this account status, so it added further weight toward viewing you as higher risk.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the overall risk was too high. To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a shorter loan term, reducing your existing debts before reapplying, or building a stronger positive payment record over the coming months. This would directly address the main reasons the application was turned down. (218 words)
